findings.title: Stored XSS via URL interpolation in imported_from footer
findings.body:
Line 13 interpolates the `url` parameter into HTML without escaping: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The `url` originates from RSS item `link`/`id` (poll_feed.rb) or the Disqus XML import (disqus.thor), and is then persisted as `post.raw` with `cook_method = :raw_html`. Because the cooking pipeline is bypassed for `:raw_html`, the raw HTML is stored verbatim and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html. A URL containing a single quote (e.g. `http://x.com/'>` attribute and injects arbitrary HTML/JS that executes inside the Discourse iframe origin. The XSS is persistent in a post authored by the configured `embed_by_username` (typically a privileged system user), giving the attacker the ability to act as that user against the Discourse API.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is not a recognized value
findings.body: Line 28 sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. ALLOWALL is not one of the standardized values (DENY, SAMEORIGIN, or the deprecated ALLOW-FROM). Browsers that don't recognize it fall back to treating the header as absent, which means the embed page can be framed by any origin on the web, not just `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The intent of the referer check is undermined because the response is now freely embeddable anywhere. The recommended replacement is a `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <embeddable_host>` header.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is set to request.referer, which can be empty
findings.body: Line 11 passes `<%= request.referer %>` as the `targetOrigin` to `parent.postMessage(...)`. The HTTP Referer header is browser-controlled and frequently null (direct navigation, referrer policies, missing header). When it is nil the rendered output becomes `parent.postMessage(..., '')`, and an empty-string targetOrigin is treated as `*` (any origin) per the HTML5 spec, leaking the iframe height to any parent window. The targetOrigin must be a fixed, server-controlled value such as the configured `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` origin, not the per-request referer.

findings.title: Origin check is a fragile substring comparison that mishandles ports
findings.body: Line 17 validates incoming postMessage events with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This requires `e.origin` to be a substring of `discourseUrl`, which is the wrong shape for an origin check. It silently rejects legitimate origins whenever the configured `discourseUrl` and the browser's `e.origin` differ by a port (e.g. `http://example.com` vs `http://example.com:8080`), and conversely accepts attackers whose origin happens to be a prefix of the configured URL. The check should compare parsed origins (e.g. `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin`) so it handles scheme/host/port correctly.

findings.title: Scheduled PollFeed job is executed synchronously inside a per-request job
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (line 41) before falling through to the HTTP fetch. PollFeed downloads the entire RSS feed and processes every item, so every embed retrieval blocks on a full feed poll. This is also a concurrency hazard: concurrent retrieves can each trigger an independent synchronous poll, the job runs without Sidekiq retry/visibility, and any failure in the feed poll propagates into the per-URL retrieve. The synchronous call should be removed (let the scheduled job do its work independently) or replaced with `Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)`.

findings.title: Race condition between TopicEmbed existence check and create
findings.body: Lines 15-30 do `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, `TopicEmbed.create!` inside `Topic.transaction`. The check and the create are not atomic: two concurrent `import` calls for the same URL both observe `embed.blank?` and both proceed to `create!`, at which point the second one raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (the migration adds a unique index on `embed_url`). The exception is not rescued, so the post is rolled back but the caller (a job or a controller) sees an error and the user-visible 'Loading...' view loops forever. Use `find_or_create_by` with a rescue, or `TopicEmbed.lock` / an upsert to serialize the create.

findings.title: embed_url column length is too small for many real URLs
findings.body: Line 6 declares `t.string :embed_url, null: false`, which Rails maps to `varchar(255)` in PostgreSQL. embed_url is the lookup key used both to find the existing embed (TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed) and as the unique index target. Real-world embed URLs with tracking query parameters or deep paths routinely exceed 255 characters, so inserts will raise `value too long for type character varying(255)` and the import will be lost. Use `t.text` (and a btree index on a hash, or a length-bounded variant) so longer URLs are not truncated or rejected.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents argument in place
findings.body: `import` appends the `imported_from` footer to `contents` via `contents << ...` (line 13). This mutates the caller's string in place. In `poll_feed.rb` the argument is `i.content` from SimpleRSS, and in `import_remote` it is `doc.content` from Readability; both are inputs the caller may still be holding. Beyond being surprising, the mutation also changes the SHA-1 of `contents` (computed on line 16 from the now-augmented string), so the content_sha1 stored in the embed reflects the appended footer rather than the imported article body. Use `contents +` or assign to a local variable.

findings.title: Stray require_dependency for unused email/sender
findings.body: Line 1 has `require_dependency 'email/sender'`, but `email/sender` is not referenced anywhere in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`. It looks like a copy/paste leftover from another job. It forces Rails to load the mailer framework on every RetrieveTopic invocation for no reason; remove it.

findings.title: NoMethodError if RSS items lack a content element
findings.body: Line 35 calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` without a nil check. RSS and Atom feeds vary: some items expose the body as `description`, `summary`, or `content:encoded`, and `i.content` is nil for items that only have one of the others. When that happens `.scrub` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the entire scheduled poll and prevents any items in the feed (including valid ones already in the loop) from being imported. Guard with `content = i.content && CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (and similarly for `i.title`).
